<!-- version: 2.48.0 -->
This update adds Schedule, a module for people who work shifts. Instead of entering the same weeks over and over, you describe the rotation once: give each kind of shift a name and a colour, then lay them onto the days of a cycle. Early, early, late, late, night, night, off, off - eight days, and it repeats from there. A fixed weekly timetable works the same way, it is just a cycle seven or fourteen days long. Single days can be replaced with a different shift or marked as a day off without disturbing the pattern.

The calendar can show these shifts as an extra layer you switch on and off, either as a small strip on the day or as a full block at its actual hours. They are never ordinary appointments and cannot be edited there - they are worked out from the pattern each time the calendar is drawn, so changing a rotation never leaves old entries behind. Every member of the household can see who is working when; changing a plan is up to that person, or an administrator. Schedule arrives switched off. An administrator turns it on under Settings, Modules.

If you record medication for someone else - a parent for a child, say - two things that did not work now do. Deleting a medication schedule and ticking off a dose both refused with "not found" for entries you had just created yourself. Ticking a dose only failed some of the time, which made it look random: it worked when you entered the dose yourself and failed once the reminder had already prepared it. Both go through the same check now.

Installed as an app on an Android tablet, Yuvomi stayed in a narrow upright strip even when the tablet was held sideways. It now follows the tablet, and whatever rotation lock you have set on it.

This version adds tables to the database for the new module. They are created automatically when the container starts; nothing needs to be done by hand, and existing data is untouched.

Full release notes are available at https://github.com/ulsklyc/yuvomi/releases/tag/v2.48.0
